text:
Olivia Chen: Quick sync — I'm proposing a new console affordance for tenant-driven API version moves: per-tenant 'migration health' + a capped opt-in slider (0-100%) that we call a 'traffic cork'. idea is to let customers opt up to X% of their traffic to v2 while we monitor.

Kevin Patel: love the name 😂 2 quick questions: how does quota accounting work during corked rollouts? do we keep v1 quotas, or run a combined reconciliation?

Maria Gomez: We should avoid double-counting for billing. Practical approach: surface a reconciliation metric and bill based on model actually served. Internally we need a short-lived mapping: tenant -> active_version -> token_usage. Then post-process to map to the customer invoice.

Sasha Ivanov: Implementation detail: runtime can tag requests with header `X-Redwood-Version-Route: v2|v1` and `X-Redwood-Rollout-Tag: tenant-<id>-cork=30`. Telemetry will then be able to compute per-version p50/p95/p99 and quota burn.

Olivia Chen: yeah the header is helpful. Console UX: show a compact card per-tenant with: migration health (0-100), p95 latency delta, error spike rate, and current cork %. Allow quick rollback.

Dave (product): can we show a projected spend delta if they move to 100% v2? even a naive estimate would help sales.

Maria Gomez: we can extrapolate from sampled traffic: sample N requests from tenant, run both v1/v2 locally or via shadowing for a minute, collect token counts and latency, multiply. Add a confidence bar.

Kevin Patel: shadowing is expensive. maybe we only sample a small percentage and extrapolate. Also need a safety: autocork triggers if p95_delta > 30% or error rate > 0.5% for 5m.

Sasha Ivanov: agree on thresholds. propose config snippet for the runtime rule:

```
rollout_policy:
  cork_enabled: true
  cork_percent: 30    # per-tenant slider
  safety_triggers:
    - metric: p95_latency_delta
      thresh_pct: 30
      window: 5m
    - metric: error_rate
      thresh_pct: 0.5
      window: 5m
  fallback: route_to: v1
```

Olivia Chen: that looks good. UX for console: slider + an 'apply as experiment' toggle. When experiment is on, show a little flame icon and a live sample of N requests. After 24h a 'migration health score' is computed: composite of latency delta, error delta, and QA eval pass rate.

Dave (product): naming suggestion: call the slider 'Safe Cork' and the experiment 'Pilot'. Product wants a tooltip: "Pilot routes up to X% of tenant traffic to the new version while monitoring safety signals."

Kevin Patel: telemetry needs new metric names. propose: `tenant.migration.health_score`, `tenant.migration.p95_delta_ms`, `tenant.migration.rollout_cork_pct`. Keep them tags on the existing request pipeline so we can slice.

Sasha Ivanov: Also add `quota.reconciliation.stale_window` flag. if a tenant toggles frequently we need to ensure we don't flip-bill. reconciliation will run hourly and export a mapping: `tenant -> {v1_tokens: n, v2_tokens: m}` for billing.

Maria Gomez: edge case: some clients don't send Accept-Version header. policy decision: default routing stays v1 unless tenant explicitly opts-in global default to v2. we should show in console whether that tenant has a 'default-version override'.

Olivia Chen: Suggest we add a migration banner in console for tenants with high traffic: "This tenant is on a Pilot. 12% traffic -> v2. Projected cost +7% if moved to 100%." clickable to open 'simulate full move'.

Kevin Patel: one more: admin API to set cork programmatically. (we'll need RBAC scope). Example: `POST /admin/tenants/:id/rollout { cork_pct: 20, mode: "pilot" }`

Sasha Ivanov: infra-bot: deploying v2-routing-change to canary pool now.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: https://deploys.redwood.internal/4387 (started) :rocket:

Maria Gomez: after we have telemetry hooking up, add a regression alert that creates a pager if `migration.health_score` drops > 20 for > 15m on a paying tenant.

Dave (product): also add a docs blurb for customers explaining why cost might change (quantization differences, larger tokenization, model architecture). short bullet list in console modal.

Olivia Chen: Action items: 1) Sasha/Kevin - add headers & metrics tags (runtime) 2) Maria - billing reconciliation plan doc 3) Dave - UX copy + projected-cost calc 4) Infra - safe canary deploy and RBAC for admin API.

Kevin Patel: I'll open the runtime PR with header switch and safety trigger.

Sasha Ivanov: I'll wire the telemetry and add the `quota.reconciliation.stale_window` flag.

Maria Gomez: I'll stub the billing job.

Dave (product): I'll draft console mocks.

Olivia Chen: thanks all. tagging for follow-up next week. :thumbsup:
